ira-calculator.formula:
Future value = P x (1 + r)^n + C x (((1 + r)^n - 1) / r)
P = current balance, C = yearly contribution, r = annual return, n = years.
Contributions are assumed at the end of each year.

keyFacts: A Traditional IRA is a US retirement account where investments grow tax-deferred until withdrawal.

ira-calculator.quickAnswer: A Traditional IRA grows tax-deferred: your balance compounds and yearly contributions add up. For example, $5,000 saved plus $6,000 a year at 7% for 20 years grows to about $265,000 - roughly $140,000 of it pure growth. Enter your numbers to project your own balance.
ira-calculator.tagline: Project the growth of a Traditional IRA with annual contributions and compound returns.
ira-calculator.workedExample:
$5,000 balance, $6,000/year, 7% return, 20 years:
1. Growth factor: 1.07^20 = 3.8697
2. Balance grows to: 5,000 x 3.8697 = $19,348
3. Contributions grow to: 6,000 x (3.8697 - 1) / 0.07 = 6,000 x 40.9957 = $245,974
4. Projected total = $19,348 + $245,974 = $265,322
5. You contributed $125,000; growth did the rest: about $140,322.
